solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: BT is showing a football match?

definitions.text: BT is showing a football match?

parts.words: BT is showing a football match?
parts.note: a broadcaster such as BT Sport televising a game live from the stadium is transmitting from away from its studios

explanation.surface: A question about what the telecoms company is screening this afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: B and T are the letters on the outside of BROADCAST, and BT (a British telecoms firm with sports channels) televising a match from the stadium is also a real example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Television coverage made on location rather than in a studio, such as a live game, is the technical term here.

clue.text: Against partner's education

parts.note: an oppo is British slang for a partner or mate, so partner's gives oppo's

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to their spouse's schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPO is British informal for a colleague or partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means being hostile or in opposition to it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Follow management on the back of a lorry

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
the board is the management of a company

explanation.surface: An instruction to trail the bosses, who are riding on the rear of a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinged flap at the rear of a truck that lets down for loading is called by this name.

clue.text: One talks of herb in rustic scene

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: talks of says we want something that is pronounced like the herb named

parts.note: dill is a feathery culinary herb

explanation.surface: Someone chattering about herbs in a country setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral idyll is a picturesque, peaceful countryside scene, often in poetry or painting.

clue.text: Clear example of fixed charge

parts.note: EX is the abbreviation in 'ex.' for example
a single flat price for everything is one rate, a fixed charge

explanation.surface: A model case of a flat-rate tariff.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to free them of blame, which is what exoneration does.

clue.text: Welcome hug

definitions.meaning: to welcome an idea is to accept it eagerly
a hug is a clasp in the arms

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting with arms open.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one adopts a proposal warmly, and one clasps a person in the arms.

clue.text: Delicate aspect of chapel finances

indicators.note: aspect of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fragile side to the church's money matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small and delicately built, like a fairy-tale sprite.

clue.text: See 1 across
Council official loses fellow in wood

indicators.note: loses tells us part of the official's title is dropped

parts.note: an alderman is a senior member of a town council
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A councillor gets lost among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' drops MAN from ALDERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alder is a tree whose timber is a wood used in furniture and guitars.

clue.text: Perpetua?

parts.note: the word perpetual with its final letter cut off; a word lacking its tail end, which also means everlasting

explanation.surface: Just a name, perhaps a saint's.
explanation.walkthrough: Perpetua looks like a saint's name, but it is 'perpetual' missing its last letter, so it is literally without its end; and perpetual means everlasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no end, and the clue word is itself missing its final letter.

clue.text: Body set up for the convenience of the monarch?

definitions.text: Body set up for the convenience of the monarch?

parts.words: Body set up for the convenience of the monarch?
parts.note: an old word for a lavatory, a convenience, so the advisers to the Crown are read as a royal toilet committee

explanation.surface: A committee formed to help the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convenience' is British for a public lavatory, as is privy; the real body is the formal group of advisers to the British sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal body of senior advisers to the British sovereign, which literally serves the Crown.

clue.text: Dispensed with posh bloke, having no time for drunk

indicators.note: having no says a letter is taken away from the posh bloke

parts.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class man
loaded is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone sacked an upper-class man and replaced him with a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no time' removes T from TOFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense with something is to get rid of it, just as one unloads an unwanted burden.

clue.text: Officer learns but gets confused

indicators.note: gets confused says the letters of the words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A junior officer studies but remains muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets confused' rearranges LEARNSBUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a British army officer below the rank of captain.

clue.text: Miserabilist notes shocking rendition of Grieg's 1st

indicators.note: a rendition of a piece renders it in a performance, here read as one word wrapped round a letter

parts.note: shocking means dire, dreadful

indicators.note: 1st says only the opening letter of the composer's name is used

explanation.surface: A gloomy musician gives a dreadful performance of the opening of a Grieg piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendition of' is a loose container signal: DIRE (shocking) is rendered round G, the 1st of Grieg's.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral lament is mournful music, the kind of tune a miserabilist would favour.

clue.text: When one goes third instead of last, letter is delivered

indicators.note: goes third instead of last tells us the named letter moves from the end to third place

parts.note: delta is a Greek letter
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A puzzle about post being handed over when the order changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes third instead of last' moves the final A of DELTA to third position.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards that have been dealt have been handed out or delivered to the players.

clue.text: Settle with all reformed gossips

indicators.note: reformed says the letters are put into a new form

explanation.surface: Pay off debts with all the reformed rumour-mongers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges SETTLE and ALL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Telltales are people who spread tales about others, a kind of busybody.

clue.text: Assessors work on sign that all can see inside

indicators.note: inside says the rating is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: to act is to work or function
Aries is a sign of the zodiac
U is the British film rating for a universal audience, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Valuers working with an astrological sign that everyone can watch.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuaries are specialists who assess insurance risks and calculate premiums.

clue.text: Betting system Aristotle invented

indicators.note: invented suggests the philosopher's name is made into something new

explanation.surface: A claim that the Greek philosopher devised a way of gambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invented' rearranges ARISTOTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser, or tote, pools all the bets on a race and divides the winnings.

clue.text: Withdrawn? Still, there's much treasure to be found within

indicators.note: to be found within says the shortened hoard sits inside the word for still

parts.note: still means motionless, inert

indicators.note: much, not all, says the treasure word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trove is a hoard of treasure

explanation.surface: A shy person has hidden riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' trims TROVE to TROV, and 'to be found within' sets it inside INERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawn person turns inward, the nature of a shy, reserved character.

clue.text: Returning French noble otherwise listed as the most soft and plump!

indicators.note: returning means the French title is read backwards

parts.note: duc is French for duke

indicators.note: otherwise says the next word is put in a different order

explanation.surface: An aristocrat coming back from France is described as very podgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns DUC into CUD; 'otherwise' rearranges LISTED into DLIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something most huggable is the softest and plumpest of its kind, like a teddy bear.

clue.text: See 9
Baby starts to encourage me — that's a sign

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: starts to says the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A child prompting the speaker, treated as an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or symbol, a sign representing a clan or idea.

clue.text: Mr Oates playing the expert

indicators.note: playing says the letters are played about with

explanation.surface: A man called Oates performing like a virtuoso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges MROATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially a distinguished conductor or musician.

clue.text: No "f" in amusement, right? That's useless

indicators.note: No says the named letter is not in the word for amusement

parts.note: fun is amusement
the letter f itself
fit means right or suitable, as in fit and proper

explanation.surface: A grumble that there is no fun at all, so the thing is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes F from FUN to leave UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not suitable for its purpose is of no use.

clue.text: Government department has suspicious meeting

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department
rum is British informal for odd or suspicious

explanation.surface: A Whitehall office holds a dodgy get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: The FO is the British Foreign Office; 'rum' means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is an assembly or gathering for public discussion.

clue.text: Bizarrely loved European city stadium

indicators.note: bizarrely says the word after it is put in a strange order

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: An Italian city's arena that was oddly cherished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarrely' rearranges LOVED into VELOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is a stadium with a banked track built for cycle racing.

clue.text: Rev needs volume and space

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: A vicar requiring a loud voice and room to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a clergyman, but it means racing an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Revving an engine makes the roaring noise that this imitative verb describes.

clue.text: Principally, Dorset controls Sandbanks

indicators.note: principally says the first letter of the word after is taken

parts.note: to own something is to control it

explanation.surface: Mostly Dorset runs Sandbanks, the wealthy peninsula near Poole.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandbanks is an exclusive spot in Dorset, a county on England's south coast; read the word as plain sandbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Downs can mean dunes or banks of sand, as along a shore.

clue.text: Roni calls about the ringing noises!

indicators.note: about says the letters of the words before are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone named Roni phones about the noise of bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RONICALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Carillons are sets of tuned bells in a tower, and the tunes they produce.

clue.text: Grab support when told

indicators.note: when told says the word is heard, not read

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue

explanation.surface: Seize something to lean on when instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to seize or wrench something away by force.

clue.text: Payment for records with hesitation during — and after

indicators.note: and after says the hesitation is repeated at the end
during says the hesitation comes in the middle of the records

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Paying for vinyl while hemming and hawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for 'with hesitation' again: the same hesitation goes both inside the records and after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A single payment of the whole amount at once, rather than instalments.

clue.text: Bingo! Changing sides is in keeping with Italian dish

indicators.note: in keeping with says the word is held within the other
changing sides swaps left for right in the game's name

parts.note: lotto is a bingo-like game of chance

explanation.surface: A cry of Bingo! and talk of switching sides fitting Italian cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Lotto is a game like bingo. The 'sides' are L (left) and R (right), giving ROTTO; 'in keeping with' is a loose container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a creamy rice dish from northern Italy.
